Author: N. Tukaramji
Bench: N. Tukaramji
 The Honourable Sri Justice N. Tukaramji
 Criminal Revision Case No.1386 Of 2008
Order:

This Criminal Revision Case has been filed under Sections 397 and 401 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short "Cr.P.C.) assailing the judgment dated 10.09.2008 in Crl.A.No.78 of 2007 passed by the V Additional Sessions Judge, (Fast Track Court) Khammam at Kothagudem, where by the conviction of the revision petitioner/appellant/accused No.2 under Section 406 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "IPC") dated 31.05.2007 in C.C.No.198 of 2003 passed by the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Yellandu, has been affirmed.
2.

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case are that:
The Mandal Revenue Officer, Garla Bayyaram issued a release order No.192756 dated 22.06.2002 in relation to food for work program of the Executive Engineer, R & B (Roads and Buildings) Department and deputed the accused No.1 who was office sub-ordinate in the Mandal Revenue Office (MRO) as route officer to deliver 300 quintals of rice, for distributing to the 2 NTR,J crlrc_1386_2008 labourers at M.L.S.
Point Garla in the fair price shop of the accused No.2 at Gandhampalli Village.

A subsequent enquiry revealed that the shop of accused No.2 has no capacity to accommodate 300 quintals of rice stock and only 20 quintals of ground stock is found in the premises, however the entries in the Issue Register-Ex.P17 was showing distribution of rice to 150 beneficiaries in serial numbers of coupons, but with 131 thumb impressions.
Basing on these improbabilities, contending that the accused Nos.1 and 2 in collusion sold away the rice in black market, the MRO lodged a complaint/Ex.P-1.

Whereupon the crime was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 409 and 420 of IPC.
3.

In trial, the MRO/complainant, the Mandal Surveyor who prepared the scene of offence sketch, the Special Deputy Collector who conducted enquiry, Neighbour to the fair price shop premises of the accused No.2, Panch for scene of offence and Constable were examined as Prosecution Witnesses (PW's) No.1 to 6 and in defence,
the accused Nos.1 and 2 got themselves 3 NTR,J crlrc_1386_2008 examined as Dw's No.1 to 2 respectively.

The trial Court on considering the material on record concluded that the though the stock register is disclosing receipt of 300 quintals of rice by the accused No.2 and the same has been distributed to the labourers, only 131 thumb impressions are found against 150 entries.

However, as the distribution is disclosing Gangavath Nagya vs The State Of A.P. on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118902885/
1 distribution of rice in the serial numbers of the coupons and the thumb impressions are apparently fictitious to the naked eye and as the enquiry of Special Deputy Collector revealed that only three names were tallied, concluded that the accused No.2 had misappropriated the 280 quintals of rice.
Therefore, convicted for the offence under Section 406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced to undergo six months simple imprisonment.

4. Against the judgment of conviction, the accused No.2 preferred an appeal vide Crl.A.No.78 of 2007 on the file of V Additional Sessions Judge (FTC), Khammam at Kothagudem, but 4 NTR,J crlrc_1386_2008 the appellate Court confirmed the judgment of the trial Court on all aspects.

sentences.text:
Thus,
the present revision.

5. Learned counsel for the revision petitioner/accused No.2 would submit that the Issue register is showing disbursement of the received rice to 150 beneficiaries against the coupons issued by the Assistant Engineer, R & B Department.
The 131 thumb impressions against 150 entries, is at the best making out that the disbursement account was not properly maintained.
Whereas to maintain the charge, the essential ingredients of misappropriation are to be established beyond reasonable doubt.

More so, when the Enquiry report/Ex.P4 of the Revenue Divisional Officer/RDO is clear that the labourers had made statement as to receipt of rice from the fair price shop, though the enquiry officer had noted that only three names were tallied.

Be that as it may, this fact is not proved before the Court by the prosecution and none of the labourers were examined or no person had lodged any complaint contending non receipt of rice against the coupon from the fair price shop.
The trial Court without considering these 5 NTR,J crlrc_1386_2008 aspects and only by the thumb marks in the issue registers straight away concluded misappropriation without conclusive evidence.

Thus, the prosecution fails to establish the charge and the accused No.2 is entitled for acquittal.
6.

On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor would submit that the trial and the appellant Courts had properly considered the materials especially the consistent evidence spoken to by the Pw's No.1 to 3 and 6.

Further, it is not the case of the accused No.2 that the premises of his shop can accommodate 300 quintals of rice and the disbursement of the huge quintals within two days and fictitious nature of thumb marks in the Issue register are sufficient to draw conclusions arrived by the Courts below, thus the prosecution had proved the case beyond doubt.
That apart the grounds urged by the revision petitioner were carefully considered by the appellate Court, thus no merit in the revision.
7. The pleadings of the learned counsel are carefully considered and the materials on record are perused.

The ingredients of criminal breach of trust as envisaged in the Section 405 of IPC requires entrustment of property or dominion over the property to the accused and the dishonest misappropriation or conversion of the property to his own use or dishonest use or disposal of the property or willfully suffering any person in violation of any direction of law or of any illegal Gangavath Nagya vs The State Of A.P. on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118902885/
2 contract.

sentences.text: In regard to entrustment of the property of 300 quintals of rice by the MRO for distribution among the beneficiaries who are labourers in food for work program, the release order to the accused No.2 who was dealer of fair price shop is not in dispute.
Further, the release order and the entries in the stock register maintained by the accused No.2 are substantiating the receipt of 300 quintals.
Therefore, placing the accused No.2 in fiduciary capacity over the property i.e., rice for the benefit of other persons/labourers has been established.
To prove gist of the acquisition, the prosecution shall prove the accused's dishonest misappropriation or conversion of the rice for own use or disposing of the entrusted property for his use.
11. In this regard the prosecution had placed the evidence of Special Deputy Collector/Pw-3 and the report/Ex.P-4.

This evidence is demonstrating that the shop of the accused No.2 is with capacity to store 100 quintals and at the time of verification ground stock of 20 quintals of rice (relevant stock)
and the issue register showing distribution of rice to 150 beneficiaries with coupon numbers in seriatim, however with the thumb impressions of only 131 persons are found.
12.

The Courts below read these facts and by noting that distribution of rice in serial number of the coupons is an improbability and the thumb impressions in the registers are seemingly alike with bare eye and the stocking capacity, held that the accused No.2 had diverted the stock and misappropriated the same.

When these aspects are carefully considered, at the outset it is not in dispute that as per the particulars in issue registers the quantum of rice distributed to 150 labourers and with the ground stock of 20 quintals is making up total stock of 300 quintals supplied and received by the accused No.2.
Genuineness of the coupons against which the rice was distributed is not in question.

Distribution of rice to the beneficiaries in exact serial number of the coupons though can be read as a improbable circumstance at the same time, a chance of distribution to the persons who come together by collecting the coupons in seriatim cannot be ruled out, like wise thumb marks found in the register could be concocted as contended by the prosecution or marking of thumb impressions by the beneficiaries as claimed by the accused No.2 cannot be brushed aside.

To establish the discrepancy beyond reasonable doubt, the prosecution should have been examined the beneficiaries whose names were recorded in the Issue register to prove that the rice was in fact not distributed or the thumb marks were not affixed by them or they are not the persons in whose names the coupons were issued.

3 14.
To note, the accused No.2 is not facing accusation that the accounted coupons were created.

Pertinently, the Special Deputy Collector/Pw-4 had mentioned that on his enquiry the labourers admitted that they have received rice from the fair price shop of accused No.2, however, certain names were not tallied.

The opinion recorded by Pw-3 cannot be taken as conclusive proof unless the prosecution establishes the fact before the Court that the names of the beneficiaries on the coupon and the persons received are different.
The prosecution at its wisdom failed to place the available best evidence.

Without such evidence, basing on the probabilities deducing adverse conclusions to the extent that of the entrusted rice has been misappropriated by the accused No.2 is neither rational nor justified.

15. In addition, mere negligence or failure to properly account register would not per se make out a case criminal breach of trust unless dishonest intention and willful omission to account for misappropriation or conversion or use or dispose of the entrusted property by the accused No.2 have been established.
For the aforesaid, it shall be held that the appellate and trial Courts had erred in appreciating the facts and law in determining the charge.
As the materials on record are giving scope to entertain reasonable doubt, the accused No.2 is entitled for benefit of doubt.
Resultantly, the judgment of appellate Court confirming the conviction and sentence are liable to be set aside.
17. In the result, this Criminal Revision Case is Allowed, and conviction and sentence recorded against the accused No.2 for the offence punishable under Section 406 of IPC is hereby set aside.
Bail bonds are cancelled.
As a sequel, the pending miscellaneous petitions are disposed of.
Date: 20.07.2023 Plp 11 NTR,J crlrc_1386_2008 THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE N. TUKARAMJI CRIMINAL REVISION CASE No.1386 OF 2008 Date: 20.07.2023.
